drafted_from: tool:fill-a-list-from-a-feed's own row (its words, input schema and sample run) in tools/fill-a-list-from-a-feed/what-this-tool-does-and-how-to-run-it.json; its sample run did not end well in the landing check, so this kit is a draft until a real run's answer is put in
start_here: Say to your AI: "Fill my list sample-feed from https://feeds.example/news, one row per entry with its title", with {"list_id": "sample-feed", "row_kind": "record:sample-feed", "feed": "https://feeds.example/news", "values": {"title": "$.title"}}. It runs tool:fill-a-list-from-a-feed and adds a row for each new entry.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it fills the list you name in list_id, and your edits to rows already there stay unless you ask for update_existing.
instructions: 1. Make the list the feed fills (for example list:sample-feed with a title field) or pick one you keep.
2. Say "Fill my list from this feed" and give the feed address and which field of an entry goes in each of the list's fields (values, as $.field paths).
3. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:fill-a-list-from-a-feed and that input; read which rows were added and which were already there.
4. Run it again later: entries already in the list are left as you edited them, unless you add "update_existing": true.

worked_examples.title: One JSON feed entry becomes one row
worked_examples.ask: Fill my sample-feed list from https://feeds.example/news.
worked_examples.given: The list list:sample-feed with one text field title, and a JSON feed at https://feeds.example/news answering {"rows": [{"id": "entry", "title": "Sample entry"}]}.
worked_examples.hands_back: The list gets one record:sample-feed row with title "Sample entry" (draft: the exact answer of a real run is not yet put in).
